currencies.name: US dollar
currencies.summary: The 1.5-year-high dollar: DXY ~102.4 on a ~2% oil surge plus hawkish Hammack — the war bid and the rate bid stacked. Dec hike ~75–85% (feed-dependent); CPI Wednesday is the test.

policy.note: Hammack: broad-based inflation, restrictive policy needed; Oct ~19–22%, Dec ~75–85%

growth.note: US resilient vs cracking Canada, soft China; oil's +2% taxes importers

inflation.note: CPI Wed 7:30am CT: 3.6% y/y, core m/m 0.2% — the deciding print

risk.note: War bid + rate bid stacked: Brent $106.65, DXY 1.5-yr high

tot.note: No direct terms-of-trade read for the dollar

positioning.note: $36bn dollar longs (wk to Oct 7), crowded into CPI — squeeze risk

currencies.name: Euro
currencies.summary: 17-month low: 1.1155, down 0.39% — squeezed by a 175bp US–Bund gap and France's 152bp spread; Stournaras pushed the ECB hike toward December.

policy.note: ECB trapped: hike this month less likely than Dec; Oct 29 odds 12%

growth.note: 2026 growth cut to 0.5% — weak, but priced; ZEW Tuesday is next

risk.note: Crude +2% is bearish for the eurozone — Europe imports most of its energy

tot.note: Brent $106.65 raises import costs for eurozone buyers

positioning.note: EUR shorts at extremes — contrarian squeeze potential favors EUR

fiscal.note: OAT–Bund 152bp widest since 2011; budget plenary Tuesday

currencies.name: British pound
currencies.summary: Sat the session out at ~$1.321 (−0.19%) — the best of the European losers, floored by ~86% November hike odds; Bailey speaks four times this week.

policy.note: BoE hawkish on hold at 3.75%; Nov 5 hike ~86% priced

growth.note: UK GDP Thu fcst −0.1% m/m — the growth counterpoint

currencies.name: Japanese yen
currencies.summary: Two-week low: USD/JPY ~158.64 (+0.21%) — crude's surge weighed and the rate gap did the rest; intervention talk caps the top.

policy.note: Rate gap favors USD: Fed 3.75–4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% — bearish JPY; BoJ Oct 30 hike only ~9% priced

risk.note: Fear bid rotated into the dollar, not the yen

tot.note: Crude +2% is a tax — Japan imports 90%+ of its energy

positioning.note: Yen longs 62,325 (wk to Oct 6); stretched-ness unquantified — neutral until the percentile feed lands

currencies.name: Swiss franc
currencies.summary: The fear gauge woke up and still fell: USD/CHF +0.54% to ~0.8347, the day's biggest USD move — the dollar won the haven race.

policy.note: SNB pinned at 0.00%; no domestic rate story

risk.note: Fear returned with the oil surge — but the dollar's haven-plus-rate bid was stronger

fiscal.note: EUR/CHF 0.9311 — French stress transmitting only lightly

currencies.name: Australian dollar
currencies.summary: Drifted to ~0.6959 (−0.36%) — the risk proxy sagged into tonight's RBA minutes at 7:30pm CT, the first real domestic input of the week.

policy.note: RBA hawkish on hold at 4.60%; minutes tonight 7:30pm CT

growth.note: China reopened soft — Golden Week consumption 'underwhelming'

risk.note: Risk-proxy read parked until the minutes

currencies.name: Canadian dollar
currencies.summary: Pinned at ~1.4282 near 18-month lows — the oil surge should have been the loonie's moment; the 161bp gap and a raging dollar kept winning.

policy.note: BoC Oct 28 hike ~25% — the hawkish-BoC thesis is broken

inflation.note: Canada CPI Oct 21 is the next inflation test

tot.note: Brent $106.65 settle; WTI ~$93.8 — the oil offset is real

note: Monday NY-close (4pm CT) edition. The ceasefire died, the rally lived: Brent settled $106.65 (+1.8%, highest since Sept 15) as the US session dismissed Trump's energy truce and bought the war premium back; DXY printed a 1.5-year high ~102.4 on crude plus hawkish Hammack. Dec hike ~75-85% (feed-dependent). FX spots are indicative index quotes. Thin holiday session (Tokyo + US bonds shut).
